title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 238 (Effect on agreement of misrepresentation or fraud by agent)

content.overview: Section 238 provides that misrepresentations made, or frauds committed, by agents acting in the course of their business for their principals, have the same effect on agreements made by such agents as if such misrepresentations or frauds had been made or committed by the principals; but misrepresentations made, or frauds committed, by agents, in matters which do not fall within their authority, do not affect their principals.
content.glance: Agent’s misrepresentation/fraud in course of business binds principal as if principal’s own; outside authority does not affect principal.
content.study: Misrepresentations made or frauds committed by agents acting in the course of their business for their principals have the same effect on agreements made by such agents as if made or committed by the principals. Misrepresentations or frauds by agents in matters outside their authority do not affect their principals. Illustration (a): an agent for sale of goods induces a buyer by an unauthorised misrepresentation — the contract is voidable at the buyer’s option as against the principal. Illustration (b): a captain signs bills of lading without having received the goods — the bills are void as between the principal and the pretended consignor. Current-law framing: identify the agent’s act; test whether it was in the course of the agent’s business for the principal and within authority; apply the same-effect rule or the outside-authority carve-out.

sections.heading: Course of business — same effect as principal
sections.body: Misrepresentation or fraud by an agent acting in the course of business for the principal has the same effect on the agreement as if done by the principal.

sections.heading: Outside authority — principal not affected
sections.body: Misrepresentation or fraud by an agent in matters not within the agent’s authority does not affect the principal.

sections.heading: Illustrations
sections.body: (a) Unauthorised misrepresentation by selling agent — contract voidable by buyer against principal. (b) Captain signs bills of lading without goods on board — bills void as between principal and pretended consignor.

provisions.title: Effect, on agreement, of misrepresentation or fraud by agent

examples.title: Unauthorised misrepresentation by selling agent
examples.body: A, being B’s agent for the sale of goods, induces C to buy them by a misrepresentation which B did not authorise. The contract is voidable as between B and C at C’s option.

examples.title: Bills of lading without goods
examples.body: A, the captain of B’s ship, signs bills of lading without having received on board the goods mentioned. The bills are void as between B and the pretended consignor.

hypotheticals.question: Does every misrepresentation by an agent bind the principal?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Only misrepresentations made in the course of the agent’s business for the principal have the same effect as the principal’s own. Matters outside authority do not affect the principal.

distinctions.title: Fraud/misrepresentation by agent (s. 238) vs principal inducing belief of authority (s. 237)
distinctions.left: Agent’s own misrepresentation/fraud in course of business
distinctions.right: Principal’s conduct inducing belief that unauthorised acts were authorised

misconceptions.trap: The principal is never bound by an agent’s fraud.
misconceptions.correction: Section 238 binds the principal where the agent acted in the course of business for the principal.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 238 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the agent’s misrepresentation or fraud. II. Test course of business and authority. III. Apply same-effect rule or outside-authority carve-out. IV. Conclude.

revisionPoints: Course of business — same effect as principal

enhancement.definition: Section 238 attributes an agent’s misrepresentation or fraud in the course of business to the principal for the purpose of the agreement, but excludes acts outside the agent’s authority.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Agent’s misrepresentation/fraud in course of business binds principal; outside authority does not.
